usage: Persist this file inside your repositories as .codescene/code-health-rules.json. Keep only the rules you want to override. A weight of 1.0 is the default, 0.5 keeps the rule active at 50% impact, 0.0 disables it. Rule sets are evaluated top-to-bottom; the first matching rule set wins and later sets are ignored (they do not merge).

rule_sets.matching_content_path_doc: Thin OS-binding shells (capture/attest/daemon shims for android, ios, macos, windows, linux, obs). These files are intentionally flat, string- and primitive-heavy passthroughs to core/ - their whole job is to gather a frame, a device name and a few scalars and hand them to core/, with no protocol logic of their own. The three module-aggregate structural metrics below are not meaningful signal for such a shell, so they are disabled for this path only. Every per-function risk rule (Complex Method, Bumpy Road Ahead, Large Method, Excess Number of Function Arguments, ...) stays active and still gates these files.

Repository-wide test-code tuning. 'Large Assertion Blocks' and 'Duplicated Assertion Blocks' are only emitted for unit-test code (their thresholds are unit_test_*), so down-weighting them never weakens application-code gating; it only reduces the weight of assertion-block noise inside the Rust inline #[cfg(test)] modules.
